topic: Relational Database SQL Queries and Joins

questions.questionText: Which of the following best defines a Database Management System (DBMS) and its primary responsibilities?
options: DBMS एक software application होती है, जिसका काम होता है, किसी भी database को manage करना
DBMS एक hardware device है जो डेटा को स्टोर करता है
DBMS एक programming language है जो केवल डेटा को पढ़ती है
DBMS एक operating system का हिस्सा है जो नेटवर्क को नियंत्रित करता है
questions.correctAnswer: DBMS एक software application होती है, जिसका काम होता है, किसी भी database को manage करना
questions.explanation: DBMS वह सॉफ्टवेयर एप्लिकेशन है जो डेटाबेस को प्रबंधित करती है, अर्थात् डेटा को जोड़ना (add), हटाना (delete), अपडेट करना (update) और खोजना (search) जैसे मुख्य कार्य करती है। अन्य विकल्प हार्डवेयर, भाषा या OS के भाग को दर्शाते हैं, जो DBMS की परिभाषा नहीं हैं।

questions.questionText: Which statement correctly describes a difference between relational and non‑relational databases and explains why SQL can be used only with relational databases?
options: Non‑relational databases enforce ACID transactions whereas relational databases do not, making SQL unnecessary for non‑relational databases.
Both relational and non‑relational databases use the same storage format, but SQL is licensed only for relational systems.
Relational databases use key‑value pairs while non‑relational databases use tables; SQL works with key‑value pairs.

Relational databases store data in tables with fixed schemas, allowing SQL to query structured data; non‑relational databases store data without tables using flexible schemas, so SQL cannot interpret their format.
questions.correctAnswer: Relational databases store data in tables with fixed schemas, allowing SQL to query structured data; non‑relational databases store data without tables using flexible schemas, so SQL cannot interpret their format.
questions.explanation: Relational databases organize data in tables (rows and columns) with a predefined schema, which matches the tabular nature of SQL statements. Non‑relational (NoSQL) databases store data in formats such as documents, key‑value pairs, or graphs without a fixed table structure, so the SQL language cannot parse or operate on that data. Hence SQL is applicable only to relational databases.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the correct SQL statement to insert a new user with id 1, name "Alice", and email "alice@example.com" into the `users` table?
options: INSERT INTO users (id, name, email) VALUES (1, 'Alice', 'alice@example.com');
INSERT INTO users (id, name, email) VALUE (1, 'Alice', 'alice@example.com');
INSERT INTO users VALUES (id=1, name='Alice', email='alice@example.com');
questions.correctAnswer: INSERT INTO users (id, name, email) VALUES (1, 'Alice', 'alice@example.com');
questions.explanation: The INSERT statement requires the keyword `INTO`, the table name, a parenthesized list of column names, the keyword `VALUES`, and a parenthesized list of corresponding values. Option 1 follows this exact syntax, while the other options have missing keywords, incorrect syntax, or use `VALUE` instead of `VALUES`.
